text:
Priya: FYI customer acme-inc hitting intermittent streaming breaks when going through an edge grpc-web / HTTP1 intermediary into our HTTP/2 frontend. Ticket: https://redwood.support/tickets/CHG-4321. Symptoms: SSE stream starts, several events, then stream stops delivering new chunks mid-event. Client reconnects and immediately receives a truncated event. Happens only when their env uses grpc-web gateway + our hosted endpoint behind the edge proxy :eyes:.

Sam: can you share a minimal repro curl or logs? grpc-web and grpc-gateway sometimes buffer or translate frames which breaks chunked flush semantics.

Priya: repro curl below (customer provided). They say calling our chat streaming endpoint with `Accept: text/event-stream` via grpc-web proxy reproduces reliably.

```bash
# repro (customer)
curl -v \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream \
  --data '{"model":"open-llm-v1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"start long stream"}]}'
```

Priya: attached excerpt of our access logs (sanitized) — you can see the request hits our frontend, then upstream GOAWAY / stream reset shortly after some bytes: 

```
[2026-03-14T18:22:53Z] request_id=abc123 client_ip=1.2.3.4 path=/v1/chat/stream proto=HTTP/2 status=200 bytes_sent=432 time_ms=12400
[2026-03-14T18:22:65Z] upstream=grpc-web-proxy error="client closed" details="incomplete chunked body"
[2026-03-14T18:22:65Z] request_id=abc123 stream_state=truncated last_chunk_size=48
```

Jordan: this matches classic intermediary buffering / translation issue. grpc-web proxies (and some API gateways) sometimes buffer the streaming response to present a single HTTP/1 response to clients, which means the origin never sees the flushes we rely on for SSE. Two likely failure modes: (1) the intermediary buffers until a content-length is known then truncates when it sees the upstream connection drop; (2) the gateway attempts to translate HTTP/2 frames to HTTP/1 chunked encoding but mishandles trailers or chunk boundaries, producing partial events.

Maya: quick checks we asked the customer to run: 
- Confirm the proxy is not setting Content-Length on the proxied response (should be chunked).
- Ensure the proxy forwards `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and doesn't synthesize `content-length`.
- Check for `X-Accel-Buffering` or equivalent buffering directives in their gateway. For nginx: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off;` or add header `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. For grpc-web wrappers, check if they have a `streaming` toggle (some implementations force buffering).

Sam: other workaround: if customers can use direct HTTP/2 (h2) from browser or client to our endpoint instead of grpc-web translation, that often avoids the problem because the transport preserves flush semantics. If not possible, a pragmatic server-side mitigation is to emit more frequent small flushes so the intermediary less likely to coalesce them — but that's a brittle workaround.

Priya: customer tried adding `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on the proxy and saw immediate improvement — fewer truncated events — but still saw occasional partial event when the proxy restarted aggressively. They can't remove the proxy.

Jordan: action items for us: 
- Confirm our frontend does not set Content-Length and always uses chunked framing + proper SSE boundaries. (I checked code path, it writes events with flush after each event.)
- Add extra logging on `stream_write` failures to capture upstream response headers (we currently log only status + bytes_sent).
- Reproduce locally with a grpc-web proxy (we should spin up `grpcwebproxy` + nginx config to replicate).

ops-bot: :rotating_light: created incident INC-2026-089 assigned to eng-runtime, priority=P2, linked: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-089

SupportBot: Noted customer billing unaffected; high user impact when reconnect loop causes token overage risk. Escalate if we confirm server-side bug.

Maya: suggestion for a medium-term fix: document recommended gateway config for streaming customers (nginx + envoy + common grpc-web wrappers) with explicit examples: disable buffering, preserve transfer-encoding, set `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, ensure no content-length is added, and prefer h2 passthrough if possible.

Sam: I'll try to reproduce end-to-end today with a grpc-web proxy + nginx -> our staging frontend. If reproducible, we should create a small harness + regression test in eng-runtime to prevent regressions. Tagging @Jordan and @Maya for visibility.

Jordan: also filing a followup issue to check our request router for any code path that might add `content-length` for small initial writes (edge case). If we find that, we'll patch and roll a canary.

Priya: customer wants ETA; I'll tell them we have an active incident (INC-2026-089) and are investigating gateway translation buffering as likely root cause. Will share workaround steps (add X-Accel-Buffering, try direct h2 if possible) and follow up when eng reproduces.

Sam: summary/resolution plan: reproduce + confirm whether intermediary is coalescing flushes or truncating chunk boundaries -> if intermediary bug, publish config docs + recommend h2 passthrough; if we find origin bug, patch + canary.

Maya: adding test notes: include a fuzz harness that randomly drops connections mid-stream to verify client reconnect behavior and that partial events are not emitted.

Priya: thanks all. I'll keep thread updated with customer feedback. :thumbsup:
